chapters.title: 📥 1. Installation & First Launch
chapters.content:
1. Installation & First Launch

1.1 Installation Process

Installing VenvHub Pro is straightforward and customizable. Launch the downloaded installer and follow the setup wizard:

  1. Select Language: Choose your installer language (you can change the application interface language at any time later).
  2. Select Installation Mode: The most crucial step. Choose between a Classic Windows Installation or unpack the software as a Portable version. Detailed differences are described below.
  3. Target Directory & Complete: Select your preferred destination folder and finish the installation.

1.2 What is the difference between Classic and Portable modes?

VenvHub Pro features smart environment detection. How the application stores configuration, downloaded QSS skins, and runtime data depends directly on your installation type.

🏢 Classic Windows Installation

Ideal for regular desktop users operating on a primary PC. The app installs into standard directories (e.g. C:\Program Files\VenvHubPro) with Start Menu shortcuts.

  • Security: Since Windows protects Program Files from unauthorized write operations, your user configuration is securely isolated.
  • Multi-user support: Multiple Windows user accounts on the same PC maintain independent settings and UI themes.

🧳 Portable (USB) Installation

Designed for developers seeking an all-in-one portable solution. The installer creates a marker file _is_portable.ini in the root folder.

  • Zero System Footprint: Leaves no trace in the Windows Registry or system directories.
  • Full Mobility: Copy the entire VenvHub Pro directory onto a USB flash drive and carry your full development environment anywhere.

1.3 Where is my data stored? (Complete Overview)

Depending on the chosen installation mode, file paths are structured as follows:

Data CategoryClassic InstallationPortable Version
Config & Themes
(venv_hub_pro_config.json, themes/)		%APPDATA%\VenvHubPro\Directly in the application directory
Local Python Runtimes
(PyRuntimes/)		C:\ProgramData\VenvHubPro\PyRuntimes
(or %LOCALAPPDATA%\VenvHubPro\PyRuntimes)		Directly in the application directory
Autostart Multi-Groups
(autostart_multi/)		%APPDATA%\VenvHubPro\autostart_multi\In assets/autostart_multi/
Temporary Files
(Downloaded Python ZIPs, etc.)		%APPDATA%\VenvHubPro\Downloads\In Downloads/

1.4 Portability, Protection & Self-Healing Engines

VenvHub Pro includes intelligent self-healing and protection engines to prevent environment corruption when moving across different PCs or changing USB drive letters.

Scenario A: Drive Letter Auto-Fix (Embed Venvs)

Automatically triggers on application startup when running in Portable mode from external drives (e.g., USB assigned as E: at home and F: at work).

  1. The app detects that it is running from drive F:.
  2. It inspects registered portable Venv paths still pointing to E:.
  3. Silently and automatically updates all drive references across configuration files and activation scripts (e.g. activate.bat).
System Venvs are protected: Standard system environments bound to host Python on C: are never altered, ensuring instant unlock upon returning to the home workstation.

Scenario B: Hardware Hash Locking (System Venvs)

If you carry a USB containing System Venvs (linked to a Python installation on your PC) to another machine (PC2) missing that exact runtime:

  1. Upon creation, VenvHub hashes the machine's ComputerHardwareId and saves it to portable_system_py.json.
  2. On PC2, the application detects the hardware mismatch.
  3. To prevent broken C-extensions and path corruption, the app completely locks execution (Play), cloning, VS Code sync, and Pip management for that environment.
Note: A locked environment is never damaged or deleted. Reconnecting the drive to the original PC immediately restores full functionality.

1.5 First Launch Setup (Setting Root Paths)

Upon initial startup, the project list will be empty. You must specify your root workspace paths:

Open the Manager window and configure these two critical paths:

  1. Projects Root:
    Click the folder icon 📁 and choose the master directory where your Python project source code lives (e.g. D:\Python_Projects).

  2. Venv Hub:
    Dedicated root directory where VenvHub Pro physically isolates and builds all virtual environments (e.g. C:\Venvs).
Single Instance Engine: The application runs strictly in single-instance mode. Subsequent launches will bring the active window to the foreground.
Best Practice: Never set 'Venv Hub' inside your Projects directory! Keep your source code cleanly separated from environment builds.
